title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## RoboRSI: Self‑Evolving Robot Framework

### The Breakthrough
RoboRSI introduces a Top‑Down Skill Refinement hierarchy that splits tasks into compound, atomic, and base skills with explicit contracts, coordinated by a Manager‑Planner‑Engineer‑Reviewer pipeline. Over 104 real‑world rounds the mobile manipulator iteratively learns multi‑object cleanup, and in simulation it achieves the highest success rates on LIBERO, LIBERO‑PRO, LIBERO‑Plus, and RoboTwin, beating the strongest baseline by 2.7‑11.0 %. This demonstrates a scalable self‑improvement loop that directly produces hardware‑ready capabilities.

### The Caveats
The paper cites simulation gains but never names concrete baselines, leaving the superiority claim unsubstantiated.

## SpatialHarness: Test‑Time Spatial Scaffolding

### The Breakthrough
SpatialHarness synchronizes an online simulation with a real robot, rendering complementary virtual camera views that augment a frozen GPT‑16 Astra policy without retraining. Interaction‑aware synchronization distinguishes static, held, and transition modes, boosting plug‑insertion success from 26.7 % to 66.7 % and achieving 0 %→100 % on a Tower of Hanoi task.

### The Caveats
Only the same frozen policy is used as a baseline; no other policies or sensor setups are compared, so universal applicability is unclear.

## VersaCamVLA: Camera‑Configurable VLA

### The Breakthrough
VersaCamVLA compresses variable‑size RGB views from any number of arbitrarily placed cameras into fixed‑size scene‑token latents, which are injected into a pretrained vision‑language‑action model via a lightweight spatial encoder. Wrist‑Augmented Pose Sampling generates diverse training poses without extra data, and experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO and a real robot show consistent gains over prior VLA methods.

### The Caveats
Robustness to arbitrary camera counts and poses is demonstrated only on the RoboTwin/LIBERO suites and a single robot, so broader applicability remains unverified.

## Dex-One2Many: One‑Demo Dexterous Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The framework converts a single human demonstration video into sequential scene graphs that provide diverse reset states and dense stage‑wise rewards, enabling reinforcement learning to train a dexterous hand in simulation and transfer zero‑shot to a real multi‑fingered hand. It improves performance by 6.5 % on seen configurations and up to 71 % on unseen scenarios across five tool‑use tasks.

### The Caveats
Performance gains are reported without baseline comparisons, making it unclear how the method stacks up against existing single‑demo or dexterous manipulation approaches.

## nano-ros: No‑Std Rust ROS2 Client

### The Breakthrough
nano-ros delivers a zero‑copy, no‑std ROS2 client written in Rust that runs on bare‑metal MCUs and RTOSes, with pluggable Zenoh, XRCE‑DDS, and Cyclone DDS backends and full pub/sub, services, actions, and parameters support. Formal verification, WCET analysis, and QEMU‑based CI enable safety‑critical embedded development.

### The Caveats
No quantitative latency or throughput measurements on actual hardware are provided, so real‑time performance claims are unverified.

## Modelship: Ray‑Backed Model Serving Cluster

### The Breakthrough
Modelship combines Ray’s distributed framework with a plug‑in loader to serve heterogeneous LLMs and diffusion models behind a unified OpenAI‑compatible REST API, adding auto‑scaling of context windows and observability via Prometheus and Grafana.

### The Caveats
Production‑ready claims lack latency, throughput, or scalability benchmarks beyond a basic OpenAI‑responses conformance check.

## Plurnk: Agentic Virtual Machine

### The Breakthrough
Plurnk gives language models addressable memory using internal URLs, letting models pull previews from many concurrent tools without exceeding attention limits, and provides a markdown‑adjacent programming language executed via sqlite+node, ANTLR, and wasm‑based parsers.

### The Caveats
Benchmark parity with a bare pi‑agent is unsupported; task details, quantitative results, and hardware specifications are missing.

## ApkClaw: LLM‑Driven Android Control

### The Breakthrough
ApkClaw links common chat platforms to an LLM that generates concrete Android UI actions, executing them via accessibility and screen‑capture APIs on a phone, with configurable back‑ends for any LLM model.

### The Caveats
No quantitative evaluation or baseline comparison is provided, so performance relative to existing mobile‑automation tools is unclear.

### Priority
RoboRSI offers the most concrete real‑world robot learning loop, turning iterative skill refinement into measurable hardware improvements.

### One action
Visit the RoboRSI repository and experiment with its Manager‑Planner‑Engineer‑Reviewer pipeline for hierarchical skill learning on your robot platform.

### What to watch
Manipulation advances span three complementary angles: SpatialHarness adds test‑time virtual views to boost fine‑grained tasks; VersaCamVLA focuses on flexible multi‑camera perception via scene‑token encoding; Dex-One2Many leverages a single human video to generate scene‑graph rewards for dexterous hands. Tracking how each method scales to broader tasks and benchmarks will reveal the most versatile approach.
